title: Combustible or Not?
description: Spark Bot 🤖 scans the academy for things that can burn. Sort combustible from non-combustible materials to earn the first ember.

content.value: Materials that CAN catch fire and burn are called COMBUSTIBLE. Materials that do NOT catch fire are called NON-COMBUSTIBLE. Knowing which is which is the first step to fire safety.

COMBUSTIBLE (can burn)     NON-COMBUSTIBLE (cannot burn)
🪵  wood                    🪨  stone
📄  paper                   🔩  iron / metal
⛽  petrol, kerosene        🧱  brick
🧵  cloth                   🥃  glass

Some combustible substances catch fire very easily and burn quickly. These are called INFLAMMABLE substances — for example petrol, alcohol, and LPG. They must be stored and handled with great care because even a tiny spark can set them alight.

Watch out: 'inflammable' does NOT mean 'cannot burn'! Inflammable means 'catches fire very easily' — the same as flammable. It's a common source of confusion, so remember: inflammable = easily catches fire.
Inflammable = flammable = catches fire EASILY. The 'in-' here does not mean 'not'. Petrol tankers carry big warning signs because petrol is highly inflammable.
Key Takeaway: Combustible materials can burn; non-combustible ones cannot. Inflammable (flammable) substances like petrol catch fire very easily and must be handled with great care.

quiz.question: A material that can catch fire and burn is called…
quiz.explain: Combustible materials, like wood and paper, can catch fire and burn.

quiz.question: Which of these is NON-combustible?
quiz.explain: Iron does not catch fire and burn easily, so it is non-combustible. Paper and cloth burn.

quiz.question: 'Inflammable' substances such as petrol are ones that…
quiz.explain: Inflammable means catches fire very easily — the 'in-' does NOT mean 'not'.
